text:
Predicates:
Twins(x) ::: x is a twin.
Triplets(x) ::: x is a triplet.
SpendTimeWithSiblings(x) ::: x spends a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings.
SameAgeSiblings(x) ::: x has siblings who are the same age.
Complain(x) ::: x complains often about annoying siblings.
LiveAtHomeRegularly(x) ::: x lives at home regularly.
DevelopBonds(x, y) ::: x develops strong bonds with y.
Luke(x) ::: x is Luke.
Premises:
∀x (Twins(x) ∨ Triplets(x) → SpendTimeWithSiblings(x)) ::: If people are twins or triplets, then they spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings.
∀x (SameAgeSiblings(x) → Twins(x) ∨ Triplets(x)) ::: If people have siblings who are the same age, then they are twins or triplets.
∀x (Complain(x) → SameAgeSiblings(x)) ::: If people complain often about annoying siblings, then they have siblings who are the same age.
∀x (¬LiveAtHomeRegularly(x) → ¬DevelopBonds(x, family)) ::: If people do not live at home regularly, then they do not develop strong bonds with their family members.
∀x (SpendTimeWithSiblings(x) → ¬LiveAtHomeRegularly(x)) ::: If people spend a lot of time hanging out with and playing with their siblings, then they often did not live at home regularly.
¬((Twins(luke) ∨ Triplets(luke)) ∧ DevelopBonds(luke, family)) → ((Twins(luke) ∨ Triplets(luke)) ⊕ DevelopBonds(luke, family)) ::: Luke is either both a twin or triplet and develops strong bonds with his family members, or he neither is a twin or triplet nor develops strong bonds with his family members.
Conclusion:
SpendTimeWithSiblings(luke) ::: Luke spends a lot of time hanging out and playing with his siblings.
